correctness.rationale: The Lie bracket [v,w]=v wedge w forces any ordinary derivation to have blocks B,f,B^[2]. The distinguished-vector alternating-bivector normal form produces C with Cv=0 and C^[2]z=z, giving a simultaneous derivation witness for the central projection S(v+z)=z even when two generator components are dependent. Conversely pair (v,v+z) forces (T-B^[2])z=C^[2]z with Cv=0; taking z=v wedge w from both factor directions shows every decomposable bivector is an eigenvector. Linearity on e_i wedge(e_j+e_k) for m>=3 makes the eigenvalues one scalar. Thus 2LocDer=Der+kS and the dimensions follow. For m=3, B -> B^[2] is invertible because char!=2, so all center-preserving maps are local, giving 27 dimensions. Independently solved modular simultaneous-witness systems over F3 for the projection S on 166 ordered pairs and exhibited a specific incompatible pair for the rank-one quotient projection Theta. Finite checks support the all-field proof, not replace it.

value.rationale: The two-point reflexive hull of derivations on the canonical free two-step nilpotent Lie family is a natural rigidity invariant. A precise one-dimensional obstruction for every m>=3, compared with the much larger one-point local hull, resolves a motivated structural distinction rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. Exact rank-three dimensions 18,19,27 concretely illustrate the two levels of locality.
residual_risks: No extension to nonlinear maps, characteristic two, or general quotient algebras is claimed.

limitations: Characteristic not two; generator rank >=3; maps k-linear.
The 2015 primary 2-local article is only abstract-inspected; historical priority is qualified.
Previously established local derivation classification for all m>=3 is credited; the new statement is specifically pairwise.
